newsitem.title: JAPAN: H.I.S. unveils broad alliance with main rival.
newsitem.headline: H.I.S. unveils broad alliance with main rival.

text.p: Japan's largest discount airline ticket seller H.I.S. Co Ltd unveiled a broad alliance with its biggest rival on Monday, paving the way for a possible merger in the future.

"The purpose of the tie-up is to establish a travel agency that is globally competitive. The tie-up is a full-scale alliance for a possible merger," H.I.S. president Hideo Sawada told a news conference.
H.I.S. and other leading companies set up a new carrier last year with the aim of becoming one of the first to enter Japan's domestic aviation market in more than 40 years.
Sawada has said the newly established Skymark Airlines will offer services in one of the country's busiest routes starting next summer. He has not specified which route that would be.
On Monday, H.I.S said that it would buy 76,000 new shares to be issued by Map International Co Ltd for a 19 percent stake in Japan's second largest discount ticket agency.
It is scheduled to buy the the shares, valued at 39.14 million yen ($334,000), on September 1.
H.I.S. also said that it would cooperate with Map over the designing and marketing of tours.
"The travel industry is facing its 'Big Bang' (deregulation), and in order to survive severe competition, a merger is one possible option," Map president Tsuyoshi Mori told the same news conference.
Sawada said that another Japanese travel agency, called Shikino Tomosha, was interested in joining the H.I.S.-Map alliance.
If Shikino Tomosha were to join the alliance, the expanded group's sales could hit 200 billion yen ($1.70 billion) this year, rising to 250 billion yen ($2.13 billion) next year, Sawada said.
"We will aim to become a travel agency that can compete in the European and U.S. markets," Sawada said. ($1=117 yen)
